clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A client who self-injects insulin at home is learning how to dispose of used needles. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will put each used needle directly into a sharps container and follow my community's disposal rules.
options.B: I can wrap loose needles in tissue and place them in the household trash after each injection.
options.C: I should flush used needles down the toilet so other people in the home cannot reach them.
options.D: I should place loose needles in the recycling bin because metal sharps can be sorted later.

semantic_correction.rationale: FDA home-sharps guidance directs consumers to place used needles and other sharps immediately into a sharps disposal container. An FDA-cleared container is preferred; if one is not available, an appropriate heavy-duty plastic household container may be acceptable under some community guidelines. Final disposal must follow local community requirements. FDA specifically advises against putting loose sharps in household trash or recycling and against flushing them down the toilet.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach home injection users to immediately contain used needles in an appropriate sharps container and follow local requirements for final disposal.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: DOs and DON'Ts of Proper Sharps Disposal
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current FDA consumer-device guidance accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Home sharps disposal DOs — immediately place used sharps in a disposal container; use an FDA-cleared container if possible; follow community disposal guidelines. DON'Ts — no loose sharps in trash or recycling and do not flush sharps down the toilet
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Home users should immediately place used sharps into a sharps disposal container and follow community disposal rules; loose sharps should not be placed in trash, recycling, or toilets.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item tests the core FDA disposal behavior without overloading the option with container-alternative details that belong in the rationale.

option_audit.A: Correct. FDA recommends immediate placement in a sharps container followed by community-compliant disposal.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. FDA advises against placing loose sharps in household or public trash.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. FDA states that sharps should not be flushed down the toilet.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. FDA states that needles and other sharps should not be placed in recycling.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows both immediate containment and final-disposal guidance.
cueing_check: All four options are first-person disposal statements of comparable length and syntax; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
